jobs.description: Assistant/Associate Professor - Accounting The Department of Business and Communication and the Accounting program at Briar Cliff University seek to fill an Assistant or Associate Professor of Accounting position to begin in Spring 2027 (preferred) or Fall 2027. This is a 9-month, tenure-eligible position focused on advancing knowledge through teaching, professional development, and service within the university community. The successful candidate will teach courses in beginning and advanced accounting, general business, and other courses that serve the University’s general education curriculum, known as the Core Values Curriculum. The typical faculty teaching load is 24 credits over the normal academic year. Collaboration with colleagues across departments and programs, and participation in curriculum development are essential to ensure the academic program remains current and rigorous. Additionally, faculty engage in professional development, complete institutional and departmental service, and advise students regarding experiential learning opportunities in addition to their coursework, supporting their professional growth and contributing to the broader educational mission. The successful candidate should have at minimum a Masters in Accounting or related field, and CPA licensure; a terminal degree in accounting or related field is preferred. The successful candidate should have demonstrated excellence in teaching at the university level, a strong record of successfully advising and mentoring students, interest in maintaining their own intellectual creativity, and an ability to contribute to curriculum development and academic service. Founded in 1930 and rooted in the Catholic Franciscan tradition, Briar Cliff University is a vibrant, values-based community dedicated to academic excellence and personal growth. Located on the scenic Loess Hills overlooking the Missouri River, "The Cliff" maintains a tight-knit learning environment with an institutional 13:1 student-to-faculty ratio. Academically, the university offers over 30 undergraduate programs and several respected graduate degrees, including regionally recognized programs in Nursing, Physical Therapy, and Sport Management. Our commitment to the student-athlete experience is equally robust; as members of the NAIA and Great Plains Athletic Conference, the Briar Cliff Chargers have earned 19 conference championships and were recently honored as an NAIA Champions of Character Gold Level institution. A city of 85,000 stretching across the corners of Iowa, South Dakota, and Nebraska (referred to as “Siouxland”), Sioux City is nestled along the Sioux River approximately 80 miles from both Omaha, NE, and Sioux Falls, SD. The city offers a vibrant, friendly community with a cost of living that is attractive for families and individuals alike. Sioux City possesses a bustling riverfront, a lively downtown arts and entertainment scene, numerous parks, and rich cultural opportunities, combining small-town charm with the amenities of a larger metropolitan area. As a regional hub for business and culture, the city features over 50 parks, the historic Orpheum Theatre, Tyson Events Center, and a mix of national retailers and award-winning local favorites. Sioux City has twice been named an “All-America City,” highlighting its strong community and significant quality of life. Interested candidates should visit the Briar Cliff University employment website for more information and to apply. Candidates should submit: A letter of interest describing the alignment of the candidate's qualifications with the position requirements Current curriculum vita A statement of teaching philosophy that addresses ways in which the candidate creates and sustains a culture of belonging, fairness and appreciation for different perspectives in the classroom Graduate and undergraduate transcripts (unofficial copies are fine at this point) Contact information (only) for three professional references For full consideration, candidates should submit their applications no later than August 31, although review of applications will continue until the position is filled. A competitive salary is commensurate with teaching experience and academic credentials. This position is subject to final budget approval.

The successful candidate should also be collaborative and execute excellent communication skills, focus on continuous learning, and share their expertise with their colleagues. jobs.description: Position Title: Professor of Information Systems and Business Analytics (ISBA) Appointment Type: Faculty Job Description: Summary of Duties and Responsibilities: The Department of Information Systems and Business Analytics (ISBA) in the Ivy College of Business at Iowa State University invites applications for a tenured position at the rank of Professor. The position includes an endowed chair for a distinguished candidate with an exceptional record of research excellence and leadership in Information Systems and Business Analytics. The position holder will demonstrate the ability to maintain an active, high-quality research program that contributes to leading journals in MIS and related fields, demonstrate effectiveness in teaching, provide leadership in advancing the department's research and academic reputation, and fulfill normal service expectations. This is a full-time, 9-month appointment beginning August 16, 2027 . A later start date may also be considered. Initial review of applications will begin on September 30, 2026 , but applications will continue to be accepted until the position is filled. The position holder will conduct high-impact scholarly research suitable for publication in leading MIS journals such as Information Systems Research , Management Information Systems Quarterly , and The Journal of Management Information Systems . The holder will also be expected to contribute to mentoring Ph.D. students, and teaching ISBA-related courses at the Ph.D. level, as well as undergraduate or Master's levels. In addition, the position holder is expected to play a key role in advancing the department's research reputation through collaboration, mentorship, and leadership, helping to further enhance the department's national and international standing in ISBA research and education. The appointment also carries the expectation of typical institutional and professional service for the rank of Professor. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. on an ongoing basis without sponsorship. Immigration sponsorship is not available for this position. Required Minimum Qualifications: Ph.D. in MIS or a closely related field An outstanding record of scholarship, eligible for a tenured position at Iowa State University An established and active record of publishing research in top-tier IS journals such as Information Systems Research , Management Information Systems Quarterly , and The Journal of Management Information Systems . Preferred Qualifications: An influential scholarly reputation, as evidenced by scholarly citations and service to the profession An active research pipeline, including papers targeted or invited for revision at premier journals Experience in mentoring junior faculty and doctoral students Experience as a full-time, tenure track or tenured faculty member A record of effective teaching of ISBA-related courses Department/Program & College Description: The Ivy College of Business at Iowa State University, established in 1984, furthers Iowa State University’s land-grant ideals by training students to be knowledgeable and ethical communicators, leaders, collaborators, and problem solvers through impactful research, innovative teaching, and community engagement. With the largest undergraduate business program in the state of Iowa and nationally ranked graduate programs, the Ivy College of Business is home to over 5000 students with a strong growth trajectory. We pride ourselves on our high ethical standards and our drive to promote an environment where all individuals may succeed academically, professionally, and personally. Each member of our community is committed to the college’s mission to link theory with practice for tomorrow’s business leaders. The college offers undergraduate, graduate, and Ph.D. programs and is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International). Less than five percent of business schools worldwide receive this accreditation. The faculty in the Department of Information Systems and Business Analytics are active in their field. They have published in premier journals such as Information Systems Research , MIS Quarterly , Journal of Management Information Systems , Management Science , the Journal of the Association for Information Systems , and Decision Sciences Journal . They serve or have served as editors, associate editors, and members of editorial boards for leading information systems journals. ISBA faculty have received doctorates from premier programs such as Arizona, Carnegie Mellon, Indiana, Northwestern University, and UT Dallas. ISBA faculty have active research projects in business analytics, cybersecurity, healthcare, IT strategy, artificial intelligence, and other IS and analytic areas. Ph.D. students graduating from the ISBA department have been placed at schools such as Notre Dame, Alabama, Oklahoma, Oklahoma State, Mississippi State, University of Cincinnati, and Florida Atlantic University. jobs.description: Position Title: Research Assistant Professor - Electrical and Computer Engineering Appointment Type: Faculty Job Description: Summary of Duties and Responsibilities: The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering ( ece.iastate.edu ), in the College of Engineering at Iowa State University, invites applications for the position of Research Assistant Professor. This is a 3-year term research faculty position that holds responsibilities primarily contributing to the research mission of the department through scholarly impact and an externally funded research program in the areas of wireless and network systems. Specifically, besides contributing to the research, education, and innovation projects led by the Center for Wireless, Communities and Innovation ( wici.iastate.edu ), the responsibilities include mentoring graduate and undergraduate students working on research and design projects. Term Faculty hold limited-term, full or part-time, renewable appointments that are not eligible for tenure, but have the potential to be reviewed for advancement into senior ranks. Research faculty must secure extramural funding to fully support their research program and at least 80% but no more than 90% of their salary, with the remainder salary provided by the department. jobs.description: Position Title: Tenure Track or Clinical Term Track Faculty Assistant-Associate-Full Professor – Radiation Oncology Appointment Type: Faculty Job Description: Summary of Duties and Responsibilities: The Department of Clinical Sciences, College of Veterinary Medicine at Iowa State University is seeking qualified applicants for a 12-month, full-time, tenured or tenure-track, or renewable clinical term-track position in Radiation Oncology. Applications are being accepted at the levels of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor. The successful candidate will be expected to be actively engaged in growing and enhancing the regional prominence of our expanding oncology program and contribute significantly to the teaching, service, and research/scholarship missions of the oncology team, including active participation in outreach activities. Excellent collaborative opportunities for research activities are available within the College of Veterinary Medicine and Iowa State University, as well as the University of Iowa Holden Comprehensive Cancer Center. The successful candidate will be joining a team that includes two medical oncologists (DACVIM), one remote radiation oncologist (DACVR-RO), four medical oncology residents, three technicians, one radiation therapist, and a local consulting team of radiation physicists. The oncology service is very active in research with multiple ongoing clinical studies in both medical and radiation oncology. The Lloyd Veterinary Medical Center is a newly constructed and renovated building providing a state-of-the-art teaching, learning, and working facility. Available equipment includes a Varian Clinac iX linear accelerator (with 120 leaf Millenium multileaf collimator and onboard imaging including cone beam CT); ARIA Record and Verify system; Varian Eclipse treatment planning system; 1.5T MRI; and helical multi-slice CT. In addition, plans for a Small Animal Cancer Clinic at the Lloyd Veterinary Medical Center are scheduled to begin construction in 2026. The Small Animal Cancer Clinic will feature dedicated Oncology workspaces, including a centralized lobby, fully equipped exam rooms, clinician and technician offices, and a designated rounds room for student teaching. This position offers a unique opportunity to grow and shape the radiation oncology program at ISU, which has a strong clinical caseload, varied teaching opportunities, and the potential to reinstitute a Radiation Oncology residency training program. The role also offers flexible opportunities to engage in additional consulting practices, enabling professional growth tailored to individual interests. At the rank of Tenured or Tenure-track Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor, the position will consist of 50- 60% on clinics/hospital service, 25-30% collaborative or independent research, 5-10% teaching professional DVM and graduate student courses, and 5% institutional service. At the rank of Clinical Term Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor, the position will consist of 75-80% on clinics/hospital service, 10- 15% collaborative or independent research, 5% teaching professional DVM and graduate student courses, and 5% institutional service. Actual percentages are flexible depending on the candidate’s expertise and departmental needs. The successful candidate will be expected to develop an active scholarly program. For appointment in the tenure-track, the selected individual should have a strong record of training and experience in radiation oncology, experience with teaching, hypothesis-driven research, and prior grant writing experience. Collaborative or independent research resulting in peer-reviewed publications and external grant submissions is expected. For an individual in the clinical term-track, scholarship could include advancing the discipline of radiation oncology through the creation and dissemination of new knowledge or participating in collaborative research.
